title: A Cache Interaction Graph for Data Locality Optimization
problem: Cache efficiency optimization and root-cause diagnosis of cache inefficiencies in programs is difficult due to complex interactions between data access patterns and cache hierarchy
motivation: Performance gap between CPUs and memory systems is critical; existing profiling tools identify bottlenecks but don't diagnose root causes
method: The approach works by tracking when data gets evicted (pushed out) from the cache and measuring how often the program reuses the same data (temporal locality) or accesses nearby memory locations together (spatial locality). It categorizes each cache miss—a failed lookup—by its root cause, whether the data was evicted too soon or accessed in a pattern mismatched to the cache structure. It then visualizes these interactions in a Cache Interaction Graph diagram and extends Cachegrind (an existing memory profiler) to analyze this down to individual variables.
key_novelty: The Cache Interaction Graph visualizes which pieces of data compete with each other in the cache, revealing the root cause of performance slowdowns.
contributions: Novel Cache Interaction Graph visualization technique
Variable-level data locality analysis with cache miss classification
Effective root-cause diagnosis methodology for cache inefficiencies
limitations: Limited to application-level profiling; overhead analysis on large-scale systems not fully explored
